extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (TC 2900) and practitioners preparing design patent drawings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and objecting to drawing disclosures in design (and general) patent applications, based on 37 CFR 1.84, 37 CFR 1.152, and MPEP §§1503.02, 1504.01(b), 608.02. Covers when to object, when to reject, and technical drawing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable categories for presenting drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two acceptable categories for presenting drawings in utility and design patents: black ink (black and white drawings) and color drawings (37 CFR 1.84(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Black-and-white (India ink or equivalent) drawings are normally required. Color drawings are permitted in design applications per 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2); when color drawings are included the specification must contain the statement: "The patent or application file contains at least one drawing executed in color...". Computer renderings are treated as drawings or photographs depending on their photorealistic nature; wireframe or line renderings are treated as line drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph usage and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs (including photocopies and computer renderings treated as photographs) may be used where they are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed subject matter (37 CFR 1.84(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs are accepted in utility and design applications in limited circumstances; if photographs are not of sufficient quality so that all details are reproducible, examiners should object and no application will be issued until acceptable photographs are submitted. Photographs submitted in lieu of ink drawings in design patent applications must be limited to the design claimed and must not disclose environmental structure (37 CFR 1.152; MPEP 1503.02(V)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawing sheets and indicia
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia should be provided on drawing sheets and, if provided, should include the application number (37 CFR 1.84(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application number has not yet been assigned, other identifying information must be provided; replacement/new sheets and annotated sheets must be labeled accordingly. Proper identification helps avoid confusion when replacement or amended drawings are filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms as separate figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be presented as separate figures and should be labeled as such (37 CFR 1.84(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label formulae/tables/waveforms as separate figures; use brackets when necessary to show relationships (e.g., common vertical axis for multiple waveforms), and ensure each waveform is clearly identified with axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper, sheet usage, and cleanliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made on paper which is flexible, strong, tear-resistant, and only one side of the sheet may be used; each sheet must be reasonably free of extraneous marks (37 CFR 1.84(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paper meeting sheet-size requirements; do not submit markings on both sides or sheets with extraneous notations that could interfere with reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded views placement and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploded views (to show relationship/order of assembly) are permissible and when an exploded view appears on the same sheet as another figure it should be placed in brackets (37 CFR 1.84(h)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brackets to embrace exploded views when on the same sheet as other figures to avoid confusion about what is part of the exploded depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarged/partial views must be separately labeled
rubrics_metrics.description: When a portion of a view is enlarged for magnification, the view and the enlarged view must each be labeled as separate views (37 CFR 1.84(h)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label enlarged detail views separately (distinct figure numbers) so they are not treated as partial views of the same figure; failure to do so is a basis for objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional view indicators and hatching
rubrics_metrics.description: The plane of a sectional view should be indicated on the view from which the section is cut by a broken line, with ends designated by numerals corresponding to the sectional view and arrows indicating direction of sight; hatching must be regularly spaced oblique parallel lines (37 CFR 1.84(h)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark broken line cutting planes with correlating numerals/letters and arrows. Use hatching (oblique lines) to indicate sectioned portions; spacing must permit clear distinction of hatch lines without difficulty. When sectional views are added in prosecution, determine whether antecedent basis exists for the hatching (new matter concern per MPEP §608.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be shown at a large enough scale to be clear when reduced to two-thirds scale for reproduction; indications such as 'Actual Size' or 'Scale ½' are not permitted (37 CFR 1.84(k)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure detail remains legible after reduction; avoid scale markings like 'Actual Size' which are disallowed. If a drawing would become illegible when reduced, enlarge it on the sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line, number, and letter quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines, numbers, and letters must be clean, black (except when drawings are in color), uniformly thick, well-defined, and heavy enough for adequate reproduction (37 CFR 1.84(l)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Durable, dark, and uniformly thick strokes are required. Poor line quality (faint, broken, uneven) is a basis for objection under 1.84(l) and may form part of a photographic/drawing quality objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading conventions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is encouraged if it aids understanding; spaced thin oblique lines preferred; shade lines must be thin, few, and contrast with the rest of the drawing; solid black shading is not permitted except to represent the color black (37 CFR 1.84(m)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use oblique line shading for contours and to show transparent/translucent/highly polished surfaces. Avoid solid black areas except to denote black color or color contrast. Improper shading may lead to objections or limitations in claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet and view numbering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheet numbers and view numbers must be plain, legible, oriented the same direction as the view; different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 and preceded by 'FIG.'; where only a single view is used, it must not be numbered nor use 'FIG.' (37 CFR 1.84(p) & (u)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number views consecutively in the order they appear on sheets when possible. Do not number a single-view drawing or use the 'FIG.' abbreviation on a single view. Maintain consistent orientation for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design drawings must comply with §1.84 and be complete
rubrics_metrics.description: The design must be represented by a drawing that complies with the requirements of §1.84 and must contain a sufficient number of views to constitute a complete disclosure of the appearance of the design (37 CFR 1.152 / MPEP 1503.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the drawing/photograph is the entire visual disclosure of the claim, it must be clear and complete; nothing regarding the design should be left to conjecture. Ensure all required views are present or that statements in the specification explicitly allow omission (e.g., 'other side is identical').

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface shading: necessity and legal risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface shading is not required but may be necessary to show character/contour of 3‑D aspects and to distinguish open vs solid areas; lack of appropriate shading in the drawing as filed may render the design non-enabling and indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) (MPEP 1503.02(II)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shading when the surface shape would otherwise be unclear. Do not apply shading to unclaimed subject matter shown in broken lines. Adding shading after filing may add new matter and present a prosecution/new matter problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oblique line shading for transparent/reflective surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Oblique line shading must be used to show transparent, translucent and highly polished or reflective surfaces, such as a mirror (MPEP 1503.02(II)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply oblique line shading specifically for these surface types to clearly indicate their visual properties; follow spacing/thin-line guidance to remain reproducible and not obscure contour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast in materials by shading/stippling to avoid color limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast in materials may be shown by using line shading in one area and stippling in another so the claim covers contrasting surfaces without being limited to colors (MPEP 1503.02(II)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use different shading techniques (lines vs stippling) to indicate material/texture contrast; this helps keep the claim from being limited to specific colors or materials unless color is intended to be claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken lines: permissible uses and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines may be used to show visible environmental structure, but may not be used to show hidden planes and surfaces that cannot be seen through opaque materials; broken lines should not be used to show unclaimed subject matter for shading purposes (37 CFR 1.152; MPEP 1503.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broken lines can indicate environment or unclaimed portions, but not hidden internal features. Do not use broken lines to portray alternate positions of components in the same view (alternate positions by full and broken lines are not permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate positions of components are prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate positions of a design component, illustrated by full and broken lines in the same view, are not permitted in a design drawing (37 CFR 1.152 / MPEP 1503.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict only the claimed appearance; do not show multiple positions in the same figure using full and broken lines. Such depictions are objectionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs and ink drawings should not be combined as formal drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs and ink drawings are not permitted to be combined as formal drawings in one application (37 CFR 1.152 / MPEP 1503.02(V)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptionally, the Office permits photos and ink drawings in the same application only to disclose separate, indistinct embodiments; combining them for the same embodiment risks inconsistencies and is strongly discouraged and a basis for objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of photographic disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If photographs are not of sufficient quality so that all details are reproducible, the examiner should object; no application will be issued until acceptable photographs are submitted and approved (MPEP 1503.02(V)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess photographic detail, appearance and shape of all features; poor reproducibility can form the basis for a 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/(b) rejection if the details are not clearly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings and ‘lined for color’ statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings are permitted in design applications when filed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2); color may also be shown by lining the surfaces for color per MPEP 608.02 and, if so, the specification should state: 'The drawings are lined for color.' (MPEP 1503.02(V)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If color drawings or color photographs are filed with the original application, color is considered an integral part of the disclosed and claimed design. Omission of color later may be permitted only if the application shows possession of the underlying configuration without color at filing (see In re Daniels). Lining entire surfaces to show color may interfere with surface shading used to define contours and can create 35 U.S.C. 112(a) issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing color on claim scope and later amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If color photographs or color drawings are filed with the original application, color will be considered an integral part of the disclosed and claimed design; omission of color later is permitted only under limited circumstances (MPEP 1503.02(V)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the original disclosure demonstrates possession of the design without color. If not, treating color as integral can limit the claim and prevent later omission of color without risking new matter or lack of possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistencies among views: objection vs rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When inconsistencies are found among the views, the examiner should object to the drawings and request that the views be made consistent. When inconsistencies are of such magnitude that the overall appearance of the design is unclear, the claim should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) (MPEP 1503.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess severity: minor drafting mistakes or inconsequential inconsistencies warrant an objection and request for corrected drawings; inconsistencies that preclude an overall understanding of the design require rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112. Use examples (toy construction vehicle, building model) to gauge threshold between objection and rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views: required types and omission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should contain a sufficient number of views to disclose the complete appearance (front, rear, top, bottom and sides); perspective views are suggested and may substitute for other views if they fully disclose surfaces. Views that are merely duplicative or flat with no ornamentation may be omitted if the specification explicitly states so (MPEP 1503.02(I)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If left and right sides are identical, provide a view of one side and state the other side is identical/mirror image. If the bottom is flat and unornamented, a bottom view may be omitted with an explicit specification statement. Avoid using the vague term 'unornamented' for visible surfaces that have structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional views: prohibition when showing internal/functional features
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectional views are not permitted when the sole purpose is to illustrate internal, functional or mechanical features; they may be included only to clarify the exterior contour when necessary (MPEP 1503.02(I)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Object to and require cancellation of sectional views that attempt to show internal construction or functional elements. If a sectional view is included to clarify exterior shape, ensure the sectional does not introduce matter lacking antecedent basis in the original disclosure (check hatching and original figures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple parts in a single article — bracket and broken-line rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If separate parts are shown in a single view, the parts must be shown embraced by a bracket '}'. If the claim involves multiple parts of a single article where the article is shown in broken lines and various parts are shown in solid lines, no bracket is needed (MPEP 1504.01(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bracket to indicate separate parts clearly when depicted together. When depicting the overall article in broken lines with solid-line parts, the bracket is unnecessary; ensure the representation matches claim drafting strategy for claiming multiple parts.
